title: Number the rows
prompt: Show each employee's name, salary, and a row number by salary from highest to lowest, as row_num. Break ties by name. Replace the ___.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC, name) AS row_num FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary, name) AS row_num FROM employees;
SELECT name, salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY name) AS row_num FROM employees;

title: RANK and ties
prompt: Show each employee's name and their rank by salary, highest first, as salary_rank, with gaps after ties.
hints: RANK gives ties the same number.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank FROM employees;
SELECT name, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank FROM employees;

title: DENSE_RANK and ties
prompt: Show each employee's name and salary level as level, with no gaps after ties, highest salary first.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS level FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS level FROM employees;
SELECT name, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary) AS level FROM employees;

title: Rank within a category
prompt: Show each product's category, name, and its price rank within its category, highest first, as price_rank.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT category, name, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) AS price_rank FROM products;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT category, name, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY price DESC) AS price_rank FROM products;
SELECT category, name, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price) AS price_rank FROM products;

title: Ties in a course
prompt: Show each graded enrolment's course_id, student_id, and rank within the course by grade, highest first, as place, with equal grades sharing a place and no gaps.
hints: Filter NULLs, then DENSE_RANK with a partition.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (15, 8, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (16, 8, 5, 55, '2024-autumn');

solutions: SELECT course_id, student_id, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY course_id ORDER BY grade DESC) AS place FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT course_id, student_id, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY course_id ORDER BY grade DESC) AS place FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL;
SELECT course_id, student_id, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY grade DESC) AS place FROM enrolments WHERE grade IS NOT NULL;

title: Fix the filter
prompt: This should show each department's highest-paid employee's name, but a window function can't go in WHERE. Fix it. Ties all count, and ignore employees with no department.
hints: Rank in a subquery, then filter outside.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET salary = 90000 WHERE id = 12;

solutions: SELECT name FROM (SELECT name, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS r FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL) WHERE r = 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM (SELECT name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC) AS r FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL) WHERE r = 1;
wrongSolutions.why: Keeps only one of any tie

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name FROM (SELECT name, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS r FROM employees WHERE department_id IS NOT NULL) WHERE r = 1;

title: Top 2 per category
prompt: Show each category and name of the 2 most expensive products in it. Use ROW_NUMBER, breaking price ties by name.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); INSERT INTO products VALUES (10, 'Vase', 'Home', 5.0, 2.0), (11, 'Bowl', 'Home', 7.0, 2.0);

solutions: SELECT category, name FROM (SELECT category, name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC, name) AS r FROM products) WHERE r <= 2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT category, name FROM (SELECT category, name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC, name) AS r FROM products) WHERE r = 2;
SELECT category, name FROM (SELECT category, name, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY price DESC, name) AS r FROM products) WHERE r <= 2;

title: Best course per student
prompt: Using a CTE with ROW_NUMBER, show each student's name and the title of their highest-graded course. Break ties by course title. Only graded enrolments count.
hints: Rank per student, join, then keep rank 1.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM enrolments; DELETE FROM courses; DELETE FROM students; INSERT INTO students VALUES (6, 'Femi', 9), (7, 'Gia', 9), (8, 'Hao', 10); INSERT INTO courses VALUES (5, 'Chemistry', 'Science'), (6, 'Drama', 'Arts'); INSERT INTO enrolments VALUES (11, 6, 5, 60, '2023-autumn'), (12, 6, 5, 60, '2024-spring'), (13, 7, 5, NULL, '2024-spring'), (14, 7, 6, 95, '2024-spring');

solutions: WITH r AS (SELECT s.name, c.title, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.id ORDER BY e.grade DESC, c.title) AS n FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id WHERE e.grade IS NOT NULL) SELECT name, title FROM r WHERE n = 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT s.name, c.title, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.id ORDER BY e.grade, c.title) AS n FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id WHERE e.grade IS NOT NULL) SELECT name, title FROM r WHERE n = 1;
SELECT s.name, c.title FROM enrolments e JOIN students s ON s.id = e.student_id JOIN courses c ON c.id = e.course_id WHERE e.grade IS NOT NULL;

title: Top 2 different salaries
prompt: Show each department's employees with one of the top 2 different salaries in that department: department name as department, employee name, and salary. Use DENSE_RANK.
hints: DENSE_RANK keeps ties, and doesn't skip a level.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET salary = 80000 WHERE id = 11; UPDATE employees SET salary = 80000 WHERE id = 12; INSERT INTO employees VALUES (16, 'Nia', 5, 11, 50000, '2024-01-01', NULL, NULL);

solutions: SELECT department, name, salary FROM (SELECT d.name AS department, e.name, e.salary, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY d.id ORDER BY e.salary DESC) AS r FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id) WHERE r <= 2;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT department, name, salary FROM (SELECT d.name AS department, e.name, e.salary, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY d.id ORDER BY e.salary DESC) AS r FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id) WHERE r <= 2;
wrongSolutions.why: A tie for first skips the second level

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT department, name, salary FROM (SELECT d.name AS department, e.name, e.salary, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY d.id ORDER BY e.salary DESC) AS r FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id) WHERE r <= 2;

title: Remove duplicates by rank
prompt: Each user sometimes has several sessions per day. For each user and day, show the id, user_id, and session_date of the longest session, breaking ties with the lowest id.
hints: ROW_NUMBER picks exactly one row per group.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM sessions; DELETE FROM users; INSERT INTO users VALUES (7, 'sable', NULL, '2024-02-27'), (8, 'tulip', 7, '2024-02-28'), (9, 'umber', 7, '2024-03-01'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 50, 'web'), (12, 7, '2024-02-29', 50, 'web'), (13, 7, '2024-03-01', 7, 'ios'), (14, 8, '2024-03-02', 33, 'android'); INSERT INTO sessions VALUES (15, 8, '2024-03-02', 90, 'ios');

solutions: SELECT id, user_id, session_date FROM (SELECT id, user_id, session_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, session_date ORDER BY minutes DESC, id) AS n FROM sessions) WHERE n = 1;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, user_id, session_date FROM (SELECT id, user_id, session_date, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY minutes DESC, id) AS n FROM sessions) WHERE n = 1;
wrongSolutions.why: One row per user, not per day

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT DISTINCT id, user_id, session_date FROM sessions;
